_note: Measured reference values, checked against: NIST Atomic Spectra Database 5.12 (ionization energies, Balmer lines), NIST Chemistry WebBook / Huber & Herzberg (diatomic constants), NIST-JANAF tables (heat capacities), JPL molecular spectroscopy catalog (CO line), NIST fluid properties (helium sound speed), NIST atomic masses, CODATA; Ciddor (air index); Czachorowski et al. 2020 (helium virial coefficients); Drake, Pachucki and others (benchmark energies).
_caveats: 16O2 B_e is not tabulated directly; 1.44563 is B_0 + alpha_e/2 from the WebBook values.
Dry-air speed of sound (343.2 m/s) is from a secondary source.
Ionization energies of one-electron ions (and Li II) in NIST ASD are theoretical QED values, not direct measurements.
NIST-JANAF heat capacities are calculated from spectroscopic constants by statistical mechanics.
Balmer 'observed' wavelengths are unresolved blends of fine-structure components about 0.009 nm apart; the uncertainty used reflects that.
H2 centrifugal distortion constant (0.0471 cm^-1, Huber & Herzberg) was not re-verified.
Helium acoustic virial coefficient is interpolated between 273.15 K and 300 K.

H electron affinity 0.754195(19) eV (Lykke, Murray, Lineberger 1991) and the H- benchmark energies (HF -0.487930, exact -0.527751017 hartree) are quoted from the literature and were not re-verified online.
NaCl: omega_e from Irikura 2007; D_0 = 4.23 +/- 0.09 eV (flame photometry / thermochemistry, 1961); dipole is the equilibrium value 8.971 D (v=0 value is 9.0012 D).
NaCl ion polarizabilities 0.179 and 3.66 A^3 are the handbook values commonly used in Rittner-type models. Modern ab initio free-ion values are 0.148 and about 5.36 A^3, so the Cl- choice matters.
H2 curve benchmark energies: Pachucki, Phys. Rev. A 82, 032509 (2010).
H2 triplet (b 3Sigma_u+) energies: Kolos & Wolniewicz, J. Chem. Phys. 43, 2429 (1965), Table VII; variational upper bounds from 1965, not checked against later work.
Magnetic shielding of H (CODATA 2022) and 3He (Pachucki 2023) are theoretical values; no direct measurement of the neutral-atom shielding exists.

Helium susceptibility: measured -2.02(7)e-6 cm^3/mol (Barter, Meisenheimer, Stevenson 1960, as quoted by Puchalski, Lesiuk, Jeziorski 2023, and tabulated in the CRC Handbook); theory -1.891035(30)e-6 (same 2023 paper). No modern precise measurement was found.

Helium dispersion: measured molar polarizability 0.5172544(10) cm^3/mol (Gaiser & Fellmuth 2018, as quoted by Puchalski et al. 2020); C6 = 1.4609778 a.u. (Yan, Babb, Dalgarno, Drake 1996, theory); well depth 10.996(4) K at 5.6080(1) bohr (Cencek et al. 2012, theory). The helium dimer itself is measured to be bound by only 151.9(13.3) neV (Zeller et al. 2016).

Helium-helium curve: Born-Oppenheimer energies from Przybytek, Cencek, Jeziorski, Szalewicz 2017 (PRL 119, 123401, Table I; the 12 bohr point is the 2012 value from the same table); theory, not measurement. Hartree-Fock limit from Kobus 1993 as tabulated in arXiv:2408.03679 (two decimals in microhartree). C8, C10 and the quadrupole and octupole polarizabilities from Yan, Babb, Dalgarno, Drake 1996 (theory). The zero crossing 4.9905 bohr is not a published number: it was interpolated from the 2017 tabulated points. Second virial coefficient at 273.16 K: measured 11.9257(15) cm^3/mol (Gaiser & Fellmuth 2019, dielectric-constant gas thermometry); theory 11.92811(13) (Czachorowski et al. 2020). Dimer: measured binding 151.9(13.3) neV (Zeller et al. 2016); best theory 138.9(5) neV and mean separation 47.13(8) angstrom (Przybytek et al. 2017). The well depth 10.996 K includes small relativistic and adiabatic corrections (0.005 K), far below the model error here.

Helium-helium components at 5.6 bohr: second-order dispersion with charge overlap -15.565 cm^-1 = -22.395 K, and the sum through second order -7.716 cm^-1; reference values from Gaussian-geminal calculations (Cencek & Szalewicz 2013) as quoted in Hapka et al., J. Mol. Model. 26, 102 (2020), Table 1. Secondary source: the primary paper was not seen.

NaCl Hartree-Fock references: molecule from NIST CCCBDB, HF/aug-cc-pVQZ (r_e 2.3958 angstrom, omega_e 356 cm^-1, dipole 9.456 D at that r_e, energy -621.458927 hartree; a large basis, not the exact Hartree-Fock limit). Atoms and ions: numerical restricted Hartree-Fock from Partridge 1987 (NASA TM 89449), ions cross-checked with Lehtola 2019; this analyzer uses unrestricted Hartree-Fock for the open-shell atoms, which can lie slightly lower. The NaCl D0 of 4.23(9) eV could not be re-verified in a source during the latest check; JANAF/CODATA enthalpies give 4.222(23) eV, consistent with it.

Cl2_constants_cm1._source: NIST Chemistry WebBook, constants of diatomic molecules, 35Cl2 X 1Sigma_g+ (read 2026-11-23)

Cl_isotopes._source: masses and natural abundances entered from memory, not checked against a table
